## Appearance

Matthew Cuthbert is an odd-looking, ungainly man with stooping shoulders and long iron-gray hair that reaches to them. He possesses kindly brown eyes that gleam with pride, alongside a full, soft brown beard that he has worn continuously since the age of twenty.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER II. Matthew Cuthbert Is Surprised P3](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0003), [v1 CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out P34](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0034)_

## Personality

Matthew Cuthbert is an exceptionally shy and reticent man who dreads interacting with women, with the exception of [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) and Mrs. [Rachel](../character/rachel-lynde.md), and harbors a specific fear of little girls. Known for his good-natured, quiet, and uncommunicative demeanor, he rarely seeks out excitement and hates being among strangers. Despite his silence, he possesses a patient and wise nature, making him a remarkably sympathetic listener. While argument is not his strong point, he holds fast to his opinions and clings to his ideas with an amazing, effective silent persistency. A deeply hardworking individual, he feels strongly about keeping [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables).

## History

Matthew Cuthbert was a quiet, shy man with a long-standing heart condition who lived at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) with his sister, [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md). Hoping to adopt a young boy to help with farm work, Matthew traveled to the [Bright River](../codex/places.md#bright-river) station only to find that an orphan girl named [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) had been sent by mistake. Enjoying her talkative nature during the ride home, he immediately developed a quiet desire to keep her. When [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) briefly confined [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to her room following an argument with [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md), Matthew secretly visited the girl and gently convinced her to apologize. Throughout Anne's youth, he continued to show her quiet affection, treating her to sweets and offering steadfast encouragement for her school activities. Observing that [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) dressed more plainly than her peers, Matthew braved his shyness to seek [Rachel](../character/rachel-lynde.md) Lynde's assistance in procuring a modern dress with puffed sleeves for Anne's Christmas performance. As the years passed, Matthew took great pride in Anne's academic achievements, including her tied first-place score on the Queen's [Entrance](../codex/places.md#entrance) exams and her eventual winning of the Avery scholarship. His health steadily declined over time, and he shared a peaceful final evening walk with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) before suddenly collapsing and dying from heart failure after reading that his and Marilla's savings were lost in the collapse of the Abbey Bank.

## Quotes

> "Well, she didn’t. She brought her. I asked the stationmaster. And I had to bring her home. She couldn’t be left there, no matter where the mistake had come in."
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P5](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0005)

> “Well now, you’ll have to punish her,” said Matthew, reaching for his hat. “I’ve nothing to do with it, remember. You warned me off yourself.”
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER XIV. Anne’s Confession P25](../source/v01-c14.md#nw-v01-c14-p0025)

> “Well now, I’m much obliged,” said Matthew, “and—and—I dunno—but I’d like—I think they make the sleeves different nowadays to what they used to be. If it wouldn’t be asking too much I—I’d like them made in the new way.”
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER XXV. Matthew Insists on Puffed Sleeves P26](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0026)

> "Just mind you that—rather than a dozen boys. Well now, I guess it wasn’t a boy that took the Avery scholarship, was it? It was a girl—my girl—my girl that I’m proud of."
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream P41](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0041)

> "I reckon she ought to be punished a little. But don’t be too hard on her, Marilla. Recollect she hasn’t ever had anyone to teach her right. You’re—you’re going to give her something to eat, aren’t you?"
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P3](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0003)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--matthew-cuthbert.md)

Matthew serves as a gentle, quiet advocate for [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) from the moment he brings her home to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables). Unlike [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md), Matthew immediately takes a liking to Anne's talkative nature and secretly encourages her, even slipping upstairs to persuade her to apologize to Mrs. [Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) so she can leave her room. He delights in spoiling her with simple treats like chocolate sweets, forming a fond friendship that helps her feel welcomed as she settles into her new life.

- Friend of — good friend who helps her grow up successfully  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXII. Anne Is Invited Out to Tea P10](../source/v01-c22.md#nw-v01-c22-p0010), [v1 CHAPTER XXIV. Miss Stacy and Her Pupils Get Up a Concert P17](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0017), [v1 CHAPTER XXXI. Where the Brook and River Meet P8](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0008)</sub>
